transcript.text: This can be as simple as the cooker supply being off or tripped, or the clock/timer being left in AUTO mode—often after a power cut—which prevents many ovens heating. First, check whether the cooker isolator switch is on and whether the cooker circuit has tripped at the consumer unit; only reset it once if it has. Then look at the clock: if it is flashing or shows AUTO, set the time and select manual mode (usually a hand symbol). Does anything on the oven work—clock, display, light or hob—and is the clock flashing or showing an AUTO/timer symbol?
Display is lit and flashing 0.00 with a little symbol. Hob works. Power went off for an hour last night. Cooker switch is on.

The hob working and the display being live show the cooker has power; many ovens lock heating out until the clock/programmer is reset after an outage. Set the clock to the current time, then cancel automatic/timed cooking and select manual mode—normally shown by a hand symbol. The exact buttons vary, but it is usually done by pressing the clock/timer buttons together, or holding the button beside the little symbol, then adjusting with +/–. Once the display is steady and manual mode is selected, try an oven function again. If it still will not heat after that, the next possibilities are the function selector or an oven heating/control fault.
ok I fiddled with it and set the time and it came on and heated. no manual though so not sure what I pressed. is that it?

Yes — that was it. The power cut reset the clock/programmer, and setting the time returned the oven to a state where it could heat again; it does not suggest a faulty oven part. If there is another outage, reset the clock first and avoid switching it off at the cooker switch unless needed, as that can reset it again. If it later will not heat even with the clock showing the correct time, that would be a separate fault.

candidates: Clock/timer left in automatic mode after a power interruption (medium)
Loss of electrical supply or tripped cooker circuit (medium)
Oven control, selector or heating fault (low)
